text:
Amy - sales: Heads-up — AcmeCorp POC next week. They run corporate TLS-inspecting proxy for outbound and want Redwood Private deployed into their VPC. They asked: can we support routing traffic through their proxy while still giving them a static egress IP for allowlist + preserve client/source IP for request-level billing?

Sandeep - solutions: Short answer: you can't have both full client IP preservation and NAT/eip-based allowlist simultaneously. If traffic goes through their inspecting proxy (which will terminate TLS), it will be a new TCP session from the proxy — original client src IP is lost unless they insert X-Forwarded-For and we trust it. We can discuss workarounds.

Olivia - netops: Options: 1) VPC Peering/Transit + customer-managed egress NAT: they keep a NAT with static EIP and we send outbound to internet directly from their NAT (no proxy). 2) PrivateLink/interface endpoint back to their proxy: our connector connects to their proxy endpoint; proxy will NAT, so no srcip preserved. 3) Deploy a small per-POC proxy in their VPC (we run a lightweight forwarder) and keep static egress EIP on our side.

Jordan - eng: Technical tradeoffs: if they require TLS inspection, their proxy will break cert pinning and end-to-end TLS for things like LLM model server trust. For model pulling/updates we need TLS passthrough. If they insist on TLS inspect for compliance, we need to exchange root certs and validate pinned cert chains. Also watch for MTU — tunnel + inspection can cause fragmentation, we've seen websocket disconnects.

Amy - sales: They're also asking about ports and the minimal allowlist for the POC. Can someone draft a small list they can give to security? They also asked if we can provide a short note for their GRC questionnaire about KMS/HSM and audit logs.

Sandeep - solutions: Minimal outbound allowlist for the POC (recommended):
- 443 TCP (model API + control plane)
- 80 TCP (http redirects) optional
- 123 UDP (NTP) if their environment blocks time sync
- 53 UDP/TCP (DNS) or provide DNS forwarding to our resolvers
- 5228-5240 TCP (gRPC/long-lived streams) *only if using streaming on dedicated routes*
Also: ensure ML model artifacts (S3/GCS endpoints) are reachable if pulling containers.

Olivia - netops: For static egress, we can provide a small pool of outbound IPs if they use our Dedicated/Reserved path. For Private (VPC) deployments, we can either: route via customer's proxy (they provide allowlist), or set up a NAT gateway in their account pointing to our connector. We cannot guarantee preservation of original src IP if the traffic traverses any NAT or proxy.

Jordan - eng: For the security questionnaire snippet:
"Redwood Private POC — security controls (short):"
- Data plane: Customer-owned VPC. Customer controls network ACLs and firewalls.
- Key management: Supports customer-managed KMS; HSM-backed KMS options available for enterprise plans.
- Auditability: Request/response metadata, per-request trace IDs, and retention-configurable logs in Console.
- TLS: We support TLS 1.2+; for Private deployments we recommend TLS passthrough for model-serving connections when customers use TLS inspection.
(If you want a formatted Q&A for their GRC team I can paste a snippet into the ticket.)

support-bot: Created POC ticket #POC-7812 and linked this thread.

Amy - sales: Perfect — Sandeep/Jordan, can you paste a concise firewall allowlist + the GRC blurb into POC-7812 by EOD? I'll send the note to their security lead and confirm whether they will do TLS-inspect or allow passthrough.

Sandeep - solutions: Will do. Also ask them whether they run an upstream TLS-bumping proxy or a transparent forward proxy. Transparent proxies may preserve client IPs via proxy protocol headers — if they can enable and we accept and validate those headers, we might be able to reconstruct source identity for logging (not for network-level srcip).

Olivia - netops: FYI — if they require SNI-based routing at the proxy, ask them to not strip SNI. If the proxy rewrites SNI we can't route to model variants correctly.

Amy - sales: Thanks all. I'll update customer and ping back once they decide on inspect vs passthrough. :thumbsup:
